Commentary.Commentary: We are back with the chase! The umpires and players are out in the middle. It will be Nur Aliya and Irdina Beh to open the innings for Malaysia Women Under-19. Rashmika Sewwandi will start with the new ball. A slip in place. Let's play...
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Given Malaysia's recent struggles with the bat, they will need to put in a remarkable performance to get anywhere close to this daunting target of 163. As for Sri Lanka, they will be hoping to start well with the ball, set the tone early, and apply constant pressure to the Malaysian batters. Back in a bit for the chase.

Dahami Sanethma is down for a quick chat. She says she is very happy with her performance and looks forward to a good tournament. Mentions that the conditions were tough and she had to dig in and bat the entire inning.

After being put into bat, Sri Lanka started strongly, thanks to an aggressive knock from Sanjana Kavindi. However, Malaysia fought back admirably, picking up two quick wickets to end the Powerplay on a positive note. Dahami Sanethma and skipper Manudi Nanayakkara steadied the ship with a promising partnership, but Malaysia broke through at a crucial juncture, lifting their spirits. Hiruni Kumari’s arrival ensured that Sri Lanka maintained momentum, with the runs flowing steadily. Hiruni perished but Dahami carried on to notch up a fifty as Sri Lanka went on to finish with 162, their highest total in Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup history.

A good fightback towards the end from Malaysia Women Under-19, conceding 28 runs from 4 overs to limit Sri Lanka Women Under-19 to 162. At one stage, it looked like they would end up with an even bigger score. As for Malaysia, it has a case of them not being able to sustain pressure for long periods but credit to them for throwing themselves around in the field.

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks break! A timely wicket for Malaysia, and they will be eager to capitalize on this breakthrough. It’s crucial for them to sharpen their efforts in the field and maintain discipline with their lines and lengths. Just as Sri Lanka seemed to be building a solid partnership, they have lost their skipper. Batting has been a concern for them in recent games, making it crucial for them to forge meaningful partnerships, with Dahami Sanethma anchoring the innings as the central figure. Hiruni Kumari walks out to bat next for Sri Lanka Women Under-19.

Commentary.Commentary: With all the pre-match formalities behind it's time for the action to take centre stage! The two umpires make their way out to the middle as Malaysia Women Under-19 burst open off their final huddle and spread across the field. Sanjana Kavindi and Sumudu Nisansala, the openers for Sri Lanka Women Under-19 make their way out to the centre. Suabika has the new ball in hand and will start the proceedings. Away we go!
Out come the match officials and the teams for national anthems. It will be Sri Lanka's anthem first followed by that of Malaysia.

PITCH REPORT - Stacy-Ann King is down at the centre for the pitch analysis. She says the overhead conditions are a bit overcast but the sun has started to peep in. Adds that the pitch looks nice and hard but could have some moisture which could assist the bowlers. Mentions that it's a 60-yard all-around boundary but with overnight rain, the ball could just plug in the outfield.

The captain of Sri Lanka Women Under-19, Manudi Nanayakkara, says that they would have bowled first as well. Adds that she is fine with batting first and they will look to put a good score on the board. Mentions that they have a good batting depth and they are really excited to get going.

Nur Dania Syuhada, the skipper of Malaysia Women Under-19, says that they will look to try and restrict the opposition to less than 120 runs and they have got a lot of learnings from the warmup games. Mentions that they are excited to showcase their talent on such a big stage and they have a few changes from the team that played the warmup games.
Malaysia Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Nur Aliya (WK), Irdina Beh, Husna, Suabika, Nur Izzatul Syafiqa, Nur Dania Syuhada (C), Nuriman, Ain, Nur Isma Dania, Nazwah, Marsya.

Sri Lanka Women Under-19 (Playing XI) - Sanjana Kavindi, Sumudu Nisansala (WK), Dahami Sanethma, Manudi Nanayakkara (C), Hiruni Kumari, Rashmika Sewwandi, Shashini Gimhani, Limansa Thilakaratne, Pramudi Methsara, Aseni Thalagune, Chamudi Praboda.
TOSS - Malaysia Women Under-19 have won the toss and they will BOWL first.

As for Sri Lanka, their campaign ended in the Super Six stage in the 2023 edition, and they will be looking to make a deeper run in the tournament this time around. Leading up to the World Cup, in the Asia Cup held here in Kuala Lumpur, they failed to make it to the semifinals. In the warm-up games before the World Cup, they lost to Bangladesh but managed to win against Samoa. These two sides also faced off in the Asia Cup, where Sri Lanka breezed past Malaysia. Manudi Nanayakkara and Co. will want to build momentum early in the tournament, especially before facing stronger sides like the West Indies and India. Stick around for the toss and team news.

How good is it for Malaysia to make their tournament debut right here at home? That should help ease some nerves. They’ve already had a taste of what to expect in the tournament. In their first warm-up game against Australia, they were bowled out for just 21, and then managed only 70 in the next game against Ireland, which was tracked down easily. For a growing side like Malaysia, captain Nur Dania Syuhada would want her team to embrace the experience, enjoy the moment, and remember that opportunities like playing in a World Cup at home don't come around every day.

Hello and welcome! The Group A action in the 2025 ICC Women's Under-19 T20 World Cup is all set to get underway as tournament hosts Malaysia face off against Sri Lanka at the Bayuemas Oval in Kuala Lumpur. It's a double-header day, with the defending champions, India, beginning their title defence later in the day at the same venue against the West Indies.
... MATCH DAY ...

The stage is set for the youngsters to shine at the ICC Women’s Under-19 T20 World Cup 2025! Match 7 kicks off at the Bayuemas Oval in Kuala Lumpur, with hosts Malaysia Women Under-19 taking on Sri Lanka Women Under-19 in their Group A opener. This match promises an intriguing battle as both teams aim to set the tone for their campaigns. The hosts, Malaysia Women Under-19, will be led by Nur Dania Syuhada, who has shown glimpses of promise with both bat and ball during the warm-up matches against tough opposition like Australia and Ireland. She will shoulder a bulk of the responsibility alongside Irdina Beh and Nuriman, who will look to step up after struggling to find consistency. On the bowling front, Syuhada will lead the charge, with Nazwah, an exciting leg-spinner, and Marsya, who showed flashes of potential, expected to play key roles. While Malaysia Women Under-19 hasn’t had the best record historically, they will be eager to put up a fight and perhaps spring an upset on home soil. The talent is there, and this exposure will only help them grow. On the other hand, Sri Lanka Women Under-19 enter the competition with a mixed bag of results from the warm-ups. After a loss to Bangladesh, they bounced back with a win over Samoa but didn’t look entirely convincing. Skipper Manudi Nanayakkara has found form with the bat, and Sanjana Kavindi has shown potential, but the team will need to address their inability to accelerate the scoring. All eyes will be on Shashini Gimhani, the 16-year-old prodigy who made headlines as the youngest player to represent the national team. With her unique ability to bowl spin with both hands, she adds an exciting X-factor to the side. Limansa Thilakaratne and Chamudi Praboda have also impressed with the ball and could be pivotal to Sri Lanka’s success. While Sri Lanka Women Under-19 enter this match as clear favourites, the hosts will be determined to make their mark and capitalize on home advantage. If Malaysia Women Under-19 can bring their A-game and keep the pressure on, they might just set the stage for an upset to kick off their campaign in style.
